extraction.name: CADS-dataset
extraction.description: A large-scale whole-body CT dataset of 22,022 volumes with annotations for 167 anatomical structures, created by integrating heterogeneous cross-institutional and cross-vendor data sources and supporting whole-body CT segmentation research.
extraction.creator: Murong Xu, Tamaz Amiranashvili, Femando Navarro, Maksym Fritsak, Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci, Suprosanna Shit, Bastian Wittmann, Sezgin Er, Sebastian M. Christ, Ezequiel de la Rosa, Julian Deseoe, Robert Graf, Hendrik Möller, Anjany Sekuboyina, Jan C. Peeken, Sven Becker, Giulia Baldini, Johannes Haubold, Felix Nensa, René Hosch, Nikhil Mirajkar, Saad Khalid, Stefan Zachow, Marc-André Weber, Georg Langs, Jakob Wasserthal, Mehmet Kemal Ozdemir, Andrey Fedorov, Ron Kikinis, Stephanie Tanadini-Lang, Jan S. Kirschke, Stephanie E. Combs, and Bjoem Menze
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was aggregated from 40 diverse sources including public archives, medical imaging challenges, focused research studies, hospital cohorts, and newly acquired/released CT collections, then systematically integrated and standardized.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Most collected scans initially lacked manual annotations; only 21% had partial annotations and 79% had no manual annotations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consisted of CT scans and annotations from public archives such as TCIA, Grand Challenge and MICCAI challenges, existing datasets including TotalSegmentator, NLST, CT-RATE, AbdomenCT-1K, Han-Seg, SAROS, VISCERAL, and newly acquired head and abdominal CT scans from hospital collaborators.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were reoriented to RAS, resampled to 1.5 mm isotropic resolution, affine matrices were simplified by removing rotation and translation components, and facial regions in newly acquired head CTs were blurred with a Gaussian filter for privacy.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were generated through a multi-stage pipeline combining existing ground-truth annotations, new manual annotations by medical research assistants and a radiation oncologist, pseudo-labeling with specialized models across nine anatomical groups, shape-informed quality control, and selection among three model flavors to assemble final labels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Pseudo-labels were analyzed using shape-informed quality control and statistical ranking of three model flavors using Dice and HD95 on in-distribution and out-of-distribution validation data, with original ground-truth annotations taking highest priority in final label assembly.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Patient age for newly acquired head CT scans (aged ≥18 years) and facial features in head CT scans, which were anonymized.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and tools are intended to advance robust AI solutions in radiology, make comprehensive anatomical analysis accessible to clinicians and researchers, and support clinical workflows such as radiation therapy planning and diagnostic radiology.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper discusses potential biases from fragmented data, class imbalance, source-specific characteristics, pseudo-label variance errors, and systematic annotation errors in existing public datasets; it also notes that excluding low-quality segmentations may remove pathological cases with atypical anatomy.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include exclusion of low-quality segmentations that may remove pathological edge cases, coverage only from head to knees, need for refinement in several structures, anonymized facial features limiting detailed facial analysis, and the current modular design rather than a unified architecture.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used to develop and train the CADS-model for whole-body CT segmentation and is intended to support further research in medical imaging, including anatomical landmark detection, cross-modality registration, anatomy-guided synthesis, longitudinal organ tracking, personalized anatomical modeling, radiation treatment planning, and large-scale population studies.

inLanguage.evidence: CADS : A Comprehensive Anatomical Dataset and Segmentation for Whole-Body Anatomy in Computed Tomography

isLiveDataset.evidence: The final aggregated dataset comprises 22 ,022 CT scans

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Our data collection strategy systematically consolidates CT scans and annotations from three main sources: (1) large-scale public archives including TotalSegmentator [27] ... (2) specialized annotation collections from medical imaging challenges ... and focused research studies ... and (3) newly contributed images and annotations

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Our data collection strategy systematically consolidates CT scans and annotations from three main sources: (1) large-scale public archives ... (2) specialized annotation collections from medical imaging challenges ... and (3) newly contributed images and annotations

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: Starting with a diverse collection of 22 ,022 CT volumes, where only 4 ,695 (21%) contain partial annotations from public sources

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: This innovative pipeline aggregates diverse CT data from over 40 sources, including public archives ( e.g., TCIA [35] and medical challenges [36,37]), along with hospital cohorts.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: The geographic diversity of the dataset spans 16 countries across multiple continents, integrating data from over 100 medical centers collected between 2007 and 2024.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: First, we reorient all images to the standard RAS (Right-Anterior-Superior) convention. Second, we resample to a uniform 1 .5 mm isotropic resolution... Third, we simplify the original affine transformation matrices by removing rotation and translation components, preserving only scaling and shear.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Our annotation methodology (Figure 2, detailed explanations available in Online Methods) first standardizes the data by aligning all images to consistent orientation and 1 .5 mm isotropic resolution. We then implement a multi-stage annotation process.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: After training the three model flavors, we determine which flavor model provides the most reliable segmentation for each target structure. We evaluate performance using both in-distribution (ID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) validation data.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: Using these carefully prepared initial training sets, we employ the nnU-Net framework [22] to train specialized models for each body group. These models then generate pseudo-labels for all 167 structures across our entire 22 ,022 CT scan collection.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: We further enhance the dataset with two new CT collections. First, we include 484 anonymized head CT scans from patients aged ≥18 years from Istanbul Medipol University

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: By making our large-scale dataset, our segmentation models, and our clinical software tool publicly available, we aim to advance robust AI solutions in radiology and make comprehensive anatomical analysis accessible to clinicians and researchers alike.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: This data-centric approach helps address healthcare data challenges such as class imbalance and potential biases while reducing overfitting risks [95].

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Despite these methodological advantages and our framework’s capabilities, we identify several directions for future research and development. (1) A primary limitation of our approach concerns the exclusion strategy in our shape-based quality assessment.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: As the foundation of our CADS framework, this large-scale collection features voxel-level annotations covering 167 anatomical structures, serving dual purposes: enabling the development of the whole-body segmentation CADS-model and supporting further research in medical imaging.
